checks.name: requirement-cursor-walk-covers-every-row-once
checks.summary: A6 on the in-memory adapter, under the SAME name the Firestore package carries: TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce. Same N=7, same two page sizes (1, and 2 which does not divide 7), same drive through Service.ListRequirementsPage, same multiset coverage assertion, same absence of any order assertion. VERDICT: `--- PASS` for both sub-walks, `ok github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/store/memory 0.003s`, and PASS again inside `make component-store-memory`. internal/store/memory/store.go is BYTE-UNCHANGED: git status shows only internal/store/memory/store_test.go modified in that package. The adapter passes because it is self-consistent, not by accident: it sorts by the raw domain id and advances with rows[start].ID.String() <= afterID, an exclusive-after over a stable total order, which is the whole of what the port promises -- and it is a DIFFERENT total order from Firestore's, which sorts by base64url of the same id. MEASURED DISAGREEMENT WITH dp-v2-079 d5, recorded rather than worked around silently: driving the identical sequence over this adapter is NOT possible with a single fixed clock. Service.transact reserves quota.ReadTransactionUsage (6,001 reads) as the worst case for every read transaction, and this adapter -- prohibited from change here -- never trues that reservation down to the reads it actually made, unlike the Firestore adapter's countReads/trueUpQuota pair. quota.DefaultBudget allows 25,000 reads per UTC day, so exactly four read transactions fit in one simulated day while a page_size=1 walk of 7 records needs seven; the first attempt failed with `daily Firestore quota reservation exceeds the hard budget: day=2023-11-14 reads=30005/25000 writes=5/10000 deletes=0/10000` at page 4. The resolution keeps the walk at full strength and weakens no assertion: the test injects a clock it advances 25 hours per page, so each read transaction lands on a fresh UTC day and quota.Counter resets its daily aggregate. That is not a sleep and not a wall clock -- the clock holds a fixed instant between explicit steps, so every run sees the identical sequence of instants -- and paging is clock-independent, so nothing the walk asserts is affected. The pre-existing absence of a true-up in this adapter is recorded here as a fact for a later task; it is not touched.

checks.name: event-cursor-walk-covers-every-row-once
checks.summary: A7 on the in-memory adapter, same single name as the Firestore package's: TestTheEventPageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryEventIsCoveredOnce. Same walk to exhaustion at page_size 1 and 2 over 7 seeded Events through the EventsPage port, same multiset coverage assertion, no order assertion. VERDICT: `--- PASS` for both sub-walks. This walk needs no clock advance because it goes through the port inside store.Transact rather than through Service.transact, so it reserves no read quota at all -- recorded so the asymmetry with the A6 walk above is not read as an inconsistency.

checks.name: the-adapter-itself-is-byte-unchanged
checks.summary: internal/store/memory/store.go is BYTE-UNCHANGED, and its test file is the only memory-side file this task touched: git status --porcelain internal/store/memory reports exactly `M internal/store/memory/store_test.go` and nothing else. internal/store/memory/source_guard_test.go is untouched. The adapter needed no fix because it is self-consistent, not because the defect spared it: both adapters satisfy the port's actual promise -- a stable total order plus exclusive-after over the very key the caller was handed -- and that promise, not a shared order, is what makes the concatenation of pages cover every record once. Measured, the two orders genuinely differ: base64url is not order-preserving, and this task's own seeded ids demonstrate it (raw req-aa < req-at, encoded cmVxLWFh > cmVxLWF0; raw ev-aa < ev-am, encoded ZXYtYWE > ZXYtYW0). That is why NO cross-adapter test here asserts an order and both assert coverage as a multiset.
